title: RCP Registry — IngredientClass
description: A governed ingredient-class entry (DECISIONS #16/#23; registry-governance guideline). Recipes reference the class id; the shopping layer resolves class to product. Entries are append-only: never deleted or repurposed — deprecate and add.

id.description: Kind-prefixed stable slug (DECISIONS #23). Never encodes display names; never changes once merged. Flour types always explicit (T65, T80…).

display_name.description: Localized display names; pt-PT culinary terms exact (massa velha ≠ isco). The id is never localized.

roles.description: Functional roles this class typically supplies (machine-read: substitution, safety, basis). Membership in the core role enum is enforced by the L2 linter against schema/rcp-core-v1.schema.json#/$defs/role — single source, not duplicated here.

density.description: Weight↔volume conversion lives per class in the catalog, never in recipes (research 00:679-684).

allergens.description: EU FIC 14 — a legal list, so a closed enum is correct (research 02:367-374).

cross_refs.description: External ontology grounding (SR-REG-005): FooDON preferred, FDC/OFF accepted. Static data — validation never performs network lookups.

label.description: The external class label exactly as published — recorded at grounding time for human review.

grounding.description: Explicit, audit-passing declaration that no external class faithfully matches (heritage items); reason goes in grounding_note.

status.description: Append-only lifecycle: deprecated entries stay resolvable forever.

canonical_recipe.description: OPTIONAL link to the document that TEACHES this preparation — the answer to 'faça um roux' when the reader has never made one. CURATION, NOT ESSENCE: many roux documents may exist (a user's own, a published one, variants); the steward picks what this entry points at, and an entry without a link stays valid forever. Distinct from `teaches`, which is prose-and-URL for human reading; this is a resolvable protocol reference. Resolution follows the published order — an explicit pin outranks the consumer's own collection, which outranks this link — so a canonical link is a DEFAULT, never an override of what the reader already has.

collection.description: REQUIRED when the link crosses collections; omitted means the registry's own corpus.

version.description: Pinned revision. Unpinned links resolve to whatever the target currently is; pinned ones report drift when it moves.
